title: The Truck
style: cinematic war film still, photorealistic, flat open desert, harsh midday light, dust haze and heat shimmer, 35mm film look, desaturated tan and olive palette, full-frame 16:9, no letterbox bars, no borders, no text or lettering anywhere in the image

CONNORS.look: Paul Connors, a lean US Army soldier in his late thirties, short brown hair, light stubble, weathered face, clear grey-blue eyes, no sunglasses or eyewear of any kind, tan camouflage combat uniform, body armor vest, combat helmet with the chin strap fastened

BOGHADAIR.look: Joseph Boghadair, a US Army machine gunner around thirty, olive skin, dark eyes, clean-shaven, no sunglasses or eyewear of any kind, close-cropped black hair, calm focused expression, tan camouflage combat uniform, body armor vest, combat helmet with the chin strap fastened

TRUCK.look: a huge yellow mining dump truck, dump bed heaped high under a lashed tan tarp; its entire front is hidden behind one flat wall of thick rusty steel plate as wide as the truck and as tall as the cab roof, covering the grille, headlights, windshield and front wheels, with a single narrow horizontal slit at driver eye height as the only opening; the steel wall wraps a short way around both sides of the cab
angles: head-on front view, the steel wall and its slit filling the frame
side view, the whole length of the truck
three-quarter rear view showing the heaped dump bed under its tarp

M2.look: an M2 .50 caliber heavy machine gun: a very large belt-fed machine gun with a long thick barrel, mounted on a pintle post, with two rear spade grips and a butterfly trigger between them, an ammunition can feeding a belt into its left side, standing on a sandbag parapet

TOWER.look: the guard tower that stands just inside the blast wall to the RIGHT of the gate in reference 1, seen close from ground level inside the base: a wooden tower about forty feet tall on four braced timber legs with a zigzag stair up one side, a large open-sided cabin on top with a plank roof on corner posts and a chest-high sandbag parapet all round, two M2 .50 caliber heavy machine guns on pintle mounts pointing out over the parapet with two soldiers behind them; the HESCO-and-sandbag blast wall and the gate visible beside it, the opening in the wall blocked by two large military cargo trucks parked nose to tail
angles: wide exterior view from the ground, the whole tower from its legs to its roof

interior view from inside the cabin: plank floor, roof posts, sandbag parapet and the two mounted heavy machine guns (reference the M2 exactly), the base's rooftops and the desert far below beyond the parapet
TOWER.life: far below, small vehicles and walking soldiers moving about the base, thin clouds drifting, a light breeze stirring dust
must: two mounted M2 heavy machine guns exactly like the M2 reference, on pintle posts with rear spade grips, pointing out over the sandbag parapet

LOCATION.look: the whole forward operating base seen from a high vantage point inside it, looking out over the gate: the high perimeter blast wall of stacked HESCO barriers and sandbags (the opening in the wall blocked by two large military cargo trucks parked nose to tail) across the middle distance with the opening at its centre blocked by two large military cargo trucks parked nose to tail, the guard tower large and clear just inside the wall to the right of the gate, dense rows of prefab huts, tents, containers and sandbag walls filling the foreground on both sides, and the straight dirt road running from the gate away across empty desert to a highway on the far horizon; in the opening there is no gate of any kind, only the two parked trucks
angles: from the top of the tower looking out over the wall: the two barrier trucks across the opening directly below, the empty road running away from them to the highway, the desert flat to the horizon; the camera is ON the tower so no tower is in frame

from the road OUTSIDE the wall, camera at road level looking away from the base toward the highway: the empty straight dirt road to the horizon, open flat desert on both sides, nothing of the base or its wall in frame
LOCATION.life: small jeeps and pickups moving slowly between the buildings, a few soldiers walking, thin clouds drifting across the sky, light dust lifting in a mild breeze
angleNotes: gate view: crop of the plate around the opening and the tower
lane view: crop of the plate's foreground
the tower and the opening, close: crop of the plate

WRECK.look: the same base after the blast, late afternoon light: the blast wall breached at the opening, the two barrier trucks blown over and burning, dozens of huts, tents and containers flattened or burning, black smoke columns, debris across the road

transform.TOWER: collapsed into a heap of splintered timber to the right of the gate, only its lower legs standing
transform.LOCATION: the same base after a huge blast: wall breached at the opening, the two barrier trucks blown over and burning, buildings flattened or burning, smoke columns

WRECK.life: smoke columns drifting, ash and dust settling, distant figures moving through the debris
angles: from ground level in the wreckage near the collapsed tower, looking across the debris toward the breached gate

geography: the base perimeter is a HIGH BLAST WALL of stacked HESCO barriers and sandbags (wire or fencing running along the top of or beside that wall is acceptable); the OPENING in the wall has NO gate panel of any kind in it - it is blocked only by EXACTLY TWO large sand-coloured military cargo trucks parked nose to tail across it as a vehicle barrier (never more than two, never a row of trucks, never none), exactly as in the LOCATION plate; seen from inside the base looking out through the gate, the dirt road runs straight away from the gate to the highway on the horizon and carries no vehicles near the gate unless a shot says otherwise (a small distant vehicle far out toward the highway is acceptable); the guard tower stands just inside the wall immediately to the RIGHT of the gate; the dense base fills the ground behind and to both sides of the gate; the truck always comes down the road from the highway toward the gate, so from the tower it approaches head-on and from the base it moves toward the camera; the bomb truck (TRUCK) is ALWAYS OUTSIDE the wall on the road beyond the barrier trucks, coming from the highway, never inside the base and never past the barrier, until the blast
